p.i: A revelation given at Kirtland, Ohio, 11 September 1831, through Joseph Smith Jr.: directions to the elders, etc.

chapter.li: LEChapter64 Verse1 Behold, thus says the Lord your God unto you, O you elders of my church: Hearken, and hear and receive my will concerning you. VerseEnd Verse2 For truly I say unto you, I will that you should overcome the world; wherefore, I will have compassion upon you. VerseEnd Verse3 There are those among you who have sinned, but truly I say, for this once, for my own glory and for the salvation of souls, I have forgiven you your sins. VerseEnd

Verse4 I will be merciful unto you, for I have given unto you the kingdom, VerseEnd Verse5 and the keys of the mysteries of the kingdom shall not be taken from my servant Joseph Smith Jr. while he lives, inasmuch as he obeys my ordinances. VerseEnd

Verse6 There are those who have sought occasion against him without a cause; VerseEnd Verse7 nevertheless, he has sinned, but truly I say unto you, I, the Lord, forgive sins unto those who confess their sins before me and ask forgiveness, who have not sinned unto death. VerseEnd Verse8 My disciples in days of old sought occasion against one another, and forgave not one another in their hearts, and for this evil they were afflicted and sorely chastened. VerseEnd Verse9 Wherefore, I say unto you that you ought to forgive one another, for he that forgives not his brother his trespasses stands condemned before the Lord, for there remains in him the greater sin. VerseEnd Verse10 I, the Lord, will forgive whom I will forgive, but of you it is required to forgive all men. VerseEnd Verse11 And you ought to say in your hearts, Let God judge between me and you, and reward you according to your deeds. VerseEnd Verse12 And he that repents not of his sins and confess them not, then you shall bring him before the church and do with him as the scriptures say unto you, either by commandment or by revelation. VerseEnd Verse13 And this you shall do that God might be glorified, not because you forgive not, having not compassion, but that you may be justified in the eyes of the law, that you may not offend him who is your lawgiver. VerseEnd Verse14 Truly I say, for this cause you shall do these things. VerseEnd

Verse15 Behold, I, the Lord, was angry with him who was my servant Ezra Booth, and also my servant Isaac Morley, for they kept not the law, neither the commandment. VerseEnd Verse16 They sought evil in their hearts, and I, the Lord, withheld my spirit. They condemned for evil that thing in which there was no evil. Nevertheless, I have forgiven my servant Isaac Morley. VerseEnd Verse17 And also my servant Edward Partridge, behold, he has sinned, and Satan seeks to destroy his soul. But when these things are made known unto them, and they repent of the evil, they shall be forgiven. VerseEnd

Verse18 And now truly I say that it is expedient in me that my servant Sidney Gilbert, after a few weeks, should return upon his business and to his agency in the land of Zion. VerseEnd Verse19 And that which he has seen and heard may be made known unto my disciples, that they perish not, and for this cause have I spoken these things. VerseEnd

Verse20 And again, I say unto you that my servant Isaac Morley may not be tempted above that which he is able to bear, and counsel wrongfully to your hurt, I gave commandment that this farm should be sold. VerseEnd Verse21 I will not that my servant Frederick G. Williams should sell his farm, for I the Lord will to retain a stronghold in the land of Kirtland for the space of five years, in the which I will not overthrow the wicked, that thereby I may save some. VerseEnd Verse22 And after that day, I, the Lord, will not hold any guilty that shall go with open hearts up to the land of Zion, for I, the Lord, require the hearts of the children of men. VerseEnd

Verse23 Behold, now it is called today (until the coming of the Son of Man), and truly it is a day of sacrifice, and a day for the tithing of my people, for he that is tithed shall not be burned at his coming, VerseEnd Verse24 for after today comes the burning. This is speaking after the manner of the Lord. For truly I say, tomorrow all the proud and they that do wickedly shall be as stubble, and I will burn them up, for I am the Lord of Hosts and I will not spare any that remain in Babylon. VerseEnd Verse25 Wherefore, if you believe me, you will labor while it is called today. VerseEnd

Verse26 And it is not meet that my servants Newel K. Whitney and Sidney Gilbert should sell their store and their possessions here, for this is not wisdom, until the residue of the church which remains in this place shall go up unto the land of Zion. VerseEnd Verse27 Behold, it is said in my laws, or forbidden, to get in debt to your enemies, VerseEnd Verse28 but behold, it is not said at any time that the Lord should not take when he please and pay as seems best to him. VerseEnd Verse29 Wherefore, as you are agents and you are on the Lord’s errand, whatever you do according to the will of the Lord is the Lord’s business. VerseEnd Verse30 And this is the Lord’s business, and he has sent you to provide for his saints in these last days, that they may obtain an inheritance in the land of Zion. VerseEnd Verse31 And behold, I, the Lord, declare unto you, and my words are sure and shall not fail, that they shall obtain it. VerseEnd Verse32 But all things must come to pass in its time. VerseEnd Verse33 Wherefore, be not weary in well doing, for you are laying the foundation of a great work, and out of small things proceeds that which is great. VerseEnd

Verse34 Behold, the Lord requires the heart and a willing mind, and the willing and obedient shall eat the good of the land of Zion in these last days. VerseEnd Verse35 And the rebellious shall be cut off out of the land of Zion, and shall be sent away, and shall not inherit the land. VerseEnd Verse36 For truly I say that the rebellious are not of the blood of Ephraim, wherefore they shall be plucked out. VerseEnd

Verse37 Behold, I, the Lord, have made my church in these last days like unto a judge sitting on a hill or in a high place, to judge the nations. VerseEnd Verse38 For it shall come to pass that the inhabitants of Zion shall judge all things pertaining to Zion, VerseEnd Verse39 and all liars and hypocrites shall be proved by them, and they which are not apostles and prophets shall be known. VerseEnd Verse40 And even the judge and his counselors, if they are not faithful in their stewardship, shall be condemned, and others shall be planted in their stead. VerseEnd Verse41 For behold, I say unto you that Zion shall flourish, and the glory of the Lord shall be upon her, VerseEnd Verse42 and she shall be an ensign unto the people. And these shall come unto her out of every nation under heaven. VerseEnd Verse43 And the days shall come when the nations of the earth shall tremble because of her, and shall fear because of her terrible ones. The Lord has spoken it, Amen. VerseEnd
